title: Holiday Social Listening Plan: Black Friday to Cyber Monday 2026
summary: A holiday social listening plan for Black Friday (Nov 27) to Cyber Monday (Nov 30), 2026: setup, alert tiers, owners, a daily command view and a review.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** A holiday social listening plan has five phases: set up queries, owners and alert tiers the week of Oct 19; rehearse alerts on a past window; freeze changes on Fri Nov 13; run a daily command view from Thanksgiving (Nov 26) to Cyber Monday (Nov 30); then review what fired and what was missed. Adobe forecasts $47.5 billion of US online spend across those five days, so the window is short and costly to get wrong (Source:[Adobe, Sept 28, 2026](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) , a forecast). The phase dates are our suggested plan, not an industry standard.


Most holiday social listening plans start on Black Friday, which is too late. By then your queries are untested, nobody owns the stock-out chatter, and the first alert lands in a channel people muted in October.


The stakes are short: Adobe forecasts that Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday will carry 17.3% of the season's US online spend, leaving little room to fix a missed signal.


This is an operating plan, not a hashtag list or a recap. It compresses setup into the week of Oct 19, then covers the calendar, risks, rehearsal, freeze, command view, tool limits and review.


## What is holiday social listening, and what does the 2026 calendar look like?


Holiday social listening is a plan, not a hashtag list: owners, alert tiers and a daily rhythm around Black Friday (Nov 27, 2026) and Cyber Monday (Nov 30, 2026).


**Holiday social listening** : listening to social conversation about your brand, competitors, promotions, stock, shipping and creators across the weeks around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, with named owners, alert tiers and a daily review rhythm. (Our definition.)

Adobe defines Cyber Week as the five days from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday, so in 2026 it runs Nov 26 to 30 (our arithmetic from the OPM and Adobe pages). **Still unannounced:** we found no 2026 Black Friday event details from Walmart or Target, and Best Buy's page lists only Nov 27.


## Why does the 2026 holiday window need its own listening plan?


A large share of the season lands in a few days, and risk themes have regulator or carrier backing. The retail figures are forecasts with different windows, so we do not combine them.


-


**Adobe (forecast, Sept 28, 2026):** $47.5 billion of US online spend over Cyber Week, 17.3% of its $275.1 billion forecast for Nov 1 to Dec 31, and discounts of up to 30% off listed price in Cyber Week. Adobe expects Cyber Monday to remain the season's biggest online shopping day, and the biggest gains in revenue share for social media and for affiliates and partners, which include social influencers. (Source:[Adobe, 2026](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


-


**Deloitte (forecast, Sept 10, 2026):** e-commerce growth of 7.5% to 8.4% for Nov 2026 to Jan 2027, against 4.0% to 4.8% for total holiday retail. (Source:[Deloitte, 2026](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/about/press-room/deloitte-forecasts-holiday-retail-sales.html) )


Four risk themes have primary sources (not legal advice).


-


**Reviews:** the FTC's Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule, effective Oct 21, 2024, prohibits writing or selling fake reviews and covers buying fake social-media indicators, such as bot followers, when the buyer knew or should have known they were fake. (Source:[FTC, 2024](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) )


-


**Price claims:** under 16 CFR 233.1, a former price in a "was/now" comparison must be a price actually offered to the public. These are guides, not rules. (Source:[16 CFR 233.1](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/233.1) )


-


**Fake stores:** the FTC's Nov 25, 2025 alert warns of scam ads for name-brand products that lead to fake sites. (Source:[FTC, 2025](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2025/11/how-avoid-online-shopping-scam-holiday-season) )


-


**Shipping:** USPS send-by dates of Dec 17 to 19 extend delivery talk past Cyber Monday.


Stock-outs, dupes and customer-care spillover had no primary source in our research, so treat them as plan assumptions.


## How do you set up, rehearse and freeze holiday social listening?


Compress setup into the week of Oct 19, rehearse for two weeks, then freeze changes on Fri Nov 13. All of this is our suggested plan.


**Setup, Mon Oct 19 to Sun Oct 25**


1.


**Name 3 to 5 decisions listening will inform** , such as pausing a promo message or answering a fake-store warning.


2.


**Seed queries by theme** from last year: our[2025 Black Friday recap](https://syncly.app/blog/black-friday-recap-trust-was-the-product) covers deal-auditor skepticism, hidden fees and returns backlash. Keep queries separate so each alert maps to an owner.


3.


**Capture baselines:** a normal week (it understates peak volume), the Oct 6 to 7 sale window, and last year's TikTok campaign window, Nov 12 to Dec 1, 2025. (Source:[TikTok, Nov 12, 2025](https://newsroom.tiktok.com/tiktok-shop-kicks-off-our-biggest-holiday-season-ever?lang=en) )


4.


**Name an owner and backup per theme** , plus a watch captain, spanning care, legal, comms, ecommerce, logistics and creators.


5.


**Define three tiers by action, not volume.** Tier 1 interrupts a named person now, Tier 2 is a same-day digest or ticket, and Tier 3 is dashboard only. Size Tier 1 with the[alert budget approach](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-alert-fatigue-how-many-alerts-is-too-many) : triage minutes divided by minutes per incident.


**Rehearsal, Mon Oct 26 to Sun Nov 8**


-


**Replay** each rule against the Oct 6 to 7 window and last year's window. Mark each would-have-fired alert act now, read later or ignore, and list stories you saw too late.


-


**Run new rules in shadow mode** for a week, sent to the author only.


-


**Tune in order:** tighten queries, group repeats, raise thresholds, then lower sensitivity.


-


**Brief care, legal and PR** on one page each: what you will send and what you need back, with a separate care route for DMs.


-


**Dry run on Thu Nov 5 or Fri Nov 6:** a 90-minute tabletop with a scripted Tier 1, such as a fake-store ad.


**Freeze, Mon Nov 9 to Sun Nov 22**


-


**Soft launch on Wed Nov 11** for TikTok Shop.


-


**Change freeze on Fri Nov 13:** no new rules, sensitivity changes or query rewrites without the watch captain's approval. Unfreeze on Wed Dec 2.


-


**Publish the on-call schedule** for Nov 23 to Dec 1, with one incident log outside the tool.


-


**Pre-approve holding statements** for stock-out, shipping delay, promotion error, fake-store warning, review accusation and safety claim.


-


**Readiness check on Mon Nov 23:** alerts reach every owner and quotas have headroom.


## What belongs in the command view from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday?


Run one screen and a fixed daily rhythm from Mon Nov 23 to Mon Nov 30. We suggest normal-plus coverage on Nov 23 to 25, on-call on Thanksgiving, a staffed rota through Sunday and full staffing on Cyber Monday, which Adobe forecasts will remain the season's biggest online shopping day. (Source:[Adobe, 2026](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) )


**Command view** : a single screen, run by a named watch captain, showing the themes, alerts, open incidents and handoffs a team needs during the peak. (Our definition.)


We suggest hourly volume against baseline, a panel per table row, a care handoff queue, an incident log and a "not in view" box for DMs.

## What must your listening tool handle at peak?


It must handle caps, quotas, report cadence and history without silently stopping. Vendor pages we read in October 2026 document limits that can stop alerts or collection.


-


**Caps:** Sprinklr's volumetric alerts can cap notifications per period; at the limit there will be "no more alerts till the time resets," which the page says can miss alert-worthy trend shifts. (Source:[Sprinklr docs](https://www.sprinklr.com/help/articles/listening-volumetric-alerts/volumetric-alert-capabilities-within-listening/645f58e80104980882a5b874) ) Determ's help center described a per-hour alert limit when we read it on Oct 12, 2026; that page now returns a 404, so confirm the setting with Determ.


-


**Quotas:** Emplifi puts a spike alert "On hold" when every query behind it has reached its mentions quota. At the yearly Listening quota, queries collect no new data until the first day of the new billing period. (Source:[Emplifi docs](https://docs.emplifi.io/platform/latest/home/crisis-management-and-spike-alerts-in-listening) )


-


**Reports:** Brand24 emails daily or weekly reports (Source:[Brand24, page dated Nov 5, 2025](https://help.brand24.com/en/articles/5336595-email-reports) ), and BrandMentions schedules emailed PDFs, with a Frequency field of weekly or monthly (Source:[BrandMentions, page dated Feb 5, 2026](https://help.brandmentions.com/en/articles/12802426-how-do-i-schedule-automated-reports-via-email) ). The pages we opened do not publish intraday scheduled reports, so the midday pulse needs a live view.


-


**Routing and baselines:** Meltwater documents routing alerts to specific teams, regions or executives. (Source:[Meltwater, as of Oct 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/products/real-time-alerting) ) Emplifi computes normal volume from historical data without publishing the method.


Vendors also use "real-time" for different clocks, so ask which one you get: our review of[what 10 vendors document](https://syncly.app/blog/real-time-social-listening-what-10-vendors-document-(2026)) separates collection cadence, ingestion latency, dashboard refresh and alert latency. The pages we opened do not publish event dashboards or shift handoff. Ask your vendor this week, and add the answers to your[social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) requirements:


1.


What happens at each cap or quota during a surge, and can it be raised for Nov 11 to Dec 1?


2.


How fast does a new query load history, and how are baselines built for holiday weeks?


3.


Can reports run more often than daily?


4.


Who can be assigned alerts, and how are departed staff removed?


## How do TikTok Shop and short-form video change the plan?


They move your start date to Nov 11 and add LIVE shopping to what you watch. TikTok says its Black Friday and Cyber Monday campaign runs Nov 11 to Nov 30 and brings shoppers, brands and creators together, and that it expects LIVE Shopping to play an even bigger role this season. (Source:[TikTok, Oct 14, 2026](https://newsroom.tiktok.com/whats-shaping-the-holiday-season-on-tiktok-shop?lang=en) )


TikTok also reports that TikTok Shop sales surpassed $500 million over the four-day 2025 Black Friday and Cyber Monday weekend (company data, not independently verified). We suggest giving the creator manager a seat, since price and disclosure accusations will likely surface in creator content (a plan assumption). Short-form mentions often skip your brand name in text; see[short-form video mentions listening misses](https://syncly.app/blog/short-form-video-mentions-social-listening-misses) . We found no TikTok statement on how LIVE-session mentions reach listening tools.


## How do you review the season afterward?


We suggest a 48-hour wash-up by Thu Dec 3, then a fuller review through Mon Dec 14, using your own data. We found no published benchmarks, so we suggest none.


-


**Measure per rule:** alerts fired and acted on, Tier 1 incidents, time to acknowledgment, stories found late, alerts ignored, and promo and price themes by day.


-


**Keep, change, kill:** record each threshold as a hypothesis with an owner and a review date.


-


**Archive** the Nov 11 to Dec 1 data and incident log as next year's replay set, after checking retention.


-


**Keep a light shipping watch** through Dec 19, then give executives a readout.


## Key Takeaways


-


Our suggested plan: set up the week of Oct 19, rehearse through Nov 8, freeze Nov 13.


-


Define tiers by action, and replay a past window before trusting any rule.


-


Audit caps, quotas, report cadence and history before the freeze.


-


Review what fired and what was missed, then archive the window.


The plan, not the software, decides whether a Tier 1 alert reaches someone who can act. Black Friday is not the start of the season; it is the day your rehearsal gets tested.
